# HEVC delayed-parameter-set hardware qualification — 2026-09-19

**AI disclosure:** This file, including its title and all prose, was generated by AI at the contributor's request.

This is the acceptance record for
[omarchy-m1-video#15](https://github.com/iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video/issues/15).
It qualifies the pending-parameter-set client patch produced by
[omarchy-m1-video#44](https://github.com/iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video/issues/44)
against the Apple M1 AVD hardware path. It does **not** say that the installed
FFmpeg package contains the patch.

## Result

| Check | Unpatched FFmpeg n9.0.1 | Selected patched FFmpeg n9.0.1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `VPSSPSPPS_A_MainConcept_1` | FAIL: 2 hardware frames, wrong checksum | **PASS: 6 hardware frames, reference checksum** |
| JCT-VC HEVC full suite | pinned r11 baseline: 144/147 | **145/147; 8,895 passing frames** |
| Pass-set comparison | — | no lost passes; one new pass |

The selected build produces all six native sizes in stream order: 176x144,
320x240, 352x288, 640x480, 704x576 and 1280x720. Its checksum is
`1ddf74263cb4953cfdfcf99c563d88ea`. The exact unpatched build reproduces the
old two-frame result at 352x288 and 1280x720 with checksum
`ec9f5857591ac4c215d194deaf52167c`.

The complete selected-client suite has two non-passes:

- `RPS_E_qualcomm_5`: 300 hardware frames at 416x240, checksum
  `b09ac8e0bd31a96d8354505d7c2ebdd5` instead of
  `c30d38bbd7ea483dc7ffe81325118e16`.
- `TSUNEQBD_A_MAIN10_Technicolor_2`: expected decode rejection before any
  frame because the stream uses unequal luma/chroma bit depths.

[`r11-comparison.json`](r11-comparison.json) compares vector names rather than
only totals. It reports `VPSSPSPPS_A_MainConcept_1` as the sole new pass, no
lost passes, no missing or extra vectors, and a successful comparison. Its
`RPS_E` category change reflects the older pass-set record's generic
`decode_error` representation; the vector remains a non-pass with its
documented r11 checksum.

## Exact client and hardware identity

The selected client is FFmpeg commit
`bf1b838f2ab88b4f8fd83443325c782ea0e0f7fa` (tag `n9.0.1`) plus
[`ffmpeg-n9.0.1-hevc-pending-parameter-sets.patch`](../../../../experiments/hevc-parameter-sets/ffmpeg-n9.0.1-hevc-pending-parameter-sets.patch),
SHA-256 `a598cbf599060ff2bb105bb95a24c5dada122b58363ad9d24337cfb1f307f26b`.
The unpatched and patched binaries were separately built and staged in local
prefixes; neither was installed system-wide. The strict checker was compiled
from driver commit `7109f7eeeba7e16c1bc5d1d5dcd96eb214d6482f` and dynamically
resolved the selected prefix's `libavformat`, `libavcodec`, `libswscale` and
`libavutil` during each candidate run.

The decoder was the installed `libva-v4l2_request-avd` 1.3.r11-2 driver on an
Apple MacBook Pro (13-inch, M1, 2020), T8103, with `linux-asahi`
7.1.13.asahi3-1. The guard can verify that the loaded module is present and the
device is idle; it cannot prove which on-disk module binary was loaded earlier
or that every patch is active. [`identities.json`](identities.json) records the
package versions, commits and SHA-256 identities, including that limitation.

## Method

The local builds enabled only the FFmpeg components needed by the strict
native-size checker and VA-API path. The essential build selection was:

```text
--disable-everything --disable-doc --disable-network --disable-autodetect
--disable-static --enable-shared --enable-ffmpeg --enable-avcodec
--enable-avformat --enable-avutil --enable-swscale
--enable-decoder=hevc,rawvideo --enable-encoder=rawvideo,wrapped_avframe
--enable-hwaccel=hevc_vaapi --enable-vaapi --enable-libdrm
--enable-parser=hevc --enable-demuxer=hevc,rawvideo
--enable-muxer=rawvideo,framemd5,null --enable-protocol=file,pipe
--enable-filter=scale,format,null,copy,showinfo,hwdownload --enable-indev=lavfi
```

Each hardware command ran through `tests/hwguard.py` with an exclusive lease,
finite deadline, AVD journal monitoring and a final idle/holder check. The
shape of the candidate full-suite command was:

```sh
env PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$FIXED_PREFIX/lib/pkgconfig" \
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$FIXED_PREFIX/lib" \
  python3 tests/hwguard.py --identity avd --deadline 3600 \
    --log fixed-hevc-guard.jsonl -- \
  python3 tests/conformance.py JCT-VC-HEVC_V1.json RESOURCES \
    --driver /usr/lib/dri --output hardware-fixed-hevc-full
```

The unpatched vector used the base prefix and `--vectors
VPSSPSPPS_A_MainConcept_1`; the patched vector used the fixed prefix and the
same selection. The helper rejects non-VA source frames in hardware mode,
preserves each decoded frame's native dimensions, hashes the cropped pixels,
and writes a schema-checked result.

Guard run IDs were:

- unpatched vector: `40fc25ab-13a7-48fd-a17e-263fc7b60365`;
- patched vector: `fc3173f5-7ef7-4a84-a486-8e6d2c6dfba3`;
- patched full suite: `0416f9da-ca2d-44b6-afd9-f2b35178bbad`.

The unpatched vector and full suite guards report `child-error` because the
conformance runner deliberately exits nonzero when any vector does not pass.
Both final records show an idle device, no timeout, no wedge and no holders;
the patched single-vector guard is `ok`.

The committed summaries remove only the voluminous per-frame arrays. They
retain every vector name, category, frame count, expected/actual checksum,
native-size set and first mismatch. The SHA-256 identities of the original
unabridged summaries are in `identities.json`.

## Acceptance and limits

- Complete-vector output and checksum: met by the six-frame guarded hardware
  pass.
- Malformed/cyclic input bounds and client regression coverage: supplied by
  merged child #44 (25 fixtures in three modes, sanitized runs, mutation
  checks, reordered streams and the complete software suite).
- Existing hardware pass set: preserved; 144/147 becomes 145/147 with no lost
  vector.
- Exact client dependency: pinned above and in the driver support matrix; the
  driver-only r11 baseline remains 144/147.
- Source/tool/device identity and scoped evidence: recorded here and in the
  adjacent machine-readable files.

Not performed: no FFmpeg package build or installation, no upstream FFmpeg
submission, no FATE sample suite, no browser/player playback qualification,
no parallel or repeated full-suite run, no other Apple Silicon device, no
kernel-module reload and no reboot. This result therefore proves a selected
local client build, not shipped end-user support.
